name: kaldrax-engineering-memory-v2
description: Curated, manually annotated engineering-memory benchmark spanning architecture, persistence, API design, reliability, security, async processing, observability, delivery, performance, frontend accessibility, testing, operations, governance, and supply-chain practices. These cases are synthetic and must not be represented as telemetry from production users.

memories.content: Decision: Keep domain workflows behind stable ports and move provider integrations into replaceable adapters.
Rule: Scope every memory query by project identifier and expose only shared records plus the requesting agent's private records.
Decision: Use SQLite write-ahead logging and a busy timeout for the local single-machine memory database.
Rule: Evolve persisted schemas with additive migrations and preserve existing rows during upgrades.
Rule: Give retryable write endpoints idempotency keys so duplicate client requests do not repeat side effects.
memories.summary: http api request retries duplicate writes

memories.content: Rule: Bound recursive retries with a maximum iteration count and an overall execution budget.
Rule: Mark session cookies Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite, and avoid storing bearer tokens in browser local storage.
Rule: Enforce authorization on the server for every protected resource; hiding a client control is not an access check.
Rule: Keep API credentials out of logs, run reports, prompts, and persistent project memory.
Rule: Validate outbound URLs and resolve host addresses before fetching user-controlled resources to prevent SSRF.
Rule: Use parameterized SQL queries and bind values instead of interpolating user input into SQL strings.
Rule: Apply per-identity rate limits and return Retry-After when a caller exceeds its request allowance.
Decision: Use opaque cursor pagination for changing datasets rather than offset pagination over mutable records.
Rule: Move messages to a dead-letter queue after the configured delivery attempts are exhausted; preserve the failure reason.
Pattern: Write domain changes and outgoing event records in one database transaction, then publish the outbox asynchronously.
Rule: Retry transient provider failures with exponential backoff and jitter; do not retry permanent validation errors.
Rule: Emit structured logs with correlation IDs and redact credentials, authorization headers, and personal data.
Rule: Propagate one trace identifier across API requests, background jobs, and provider calls.
Decision: Alert on user-visible service-level objective burn rate rather than raw host CPU thresholds alone.
Rule: Expose separate liveness and readiness checks; readiness must fail when required dependencies are unavailable.
Rule: Keep the previous release artifact available and automatically roll back when post-deploy health checks fail.
Rule: Pin runtime and tool versions in CI, install from the lock file, and run the same checks on every supported Python version.
Rule: Define cache invalidation and ownership before adding a cache; stale authorization and configuration must not be served.
Rule: Use query plans and production-shaped data to choose indexes; avoid indexing every column without evidence.
Rule: Batch embedding requests and cap batch size to reduce local model overhead without exceeding memory limits.
Rule: All interactive controls must be reachable and operable with a keyboard and expose visible focus state.
Rule: Meet WCAG AA text contrast targets and never communicate status by color alone.
Decision: Validate inbound and outbound API payloads against a versioned schema at the system boundary.
Pattern: Use property-based tests for parser invariants and boundary-heavy input spaces in addition to example-based tests.
Rule: Run backward-compatibility tests against the oldest supported database schema before releasing migrations.
Rule: Verify backups by restoring them in a scheduled drill; a successful backup job alone does not prove recoverability.
Rule: Put risky releases behind a remotely configurable feature flag with an emergency kill switch.
Decision: Record architecture decisions with context, alternatives, consequences, status, and a stable identifier.
Rule: Pin direct dependencies, review transitive updates, and generate an SBOM for release artifacts.
Rule: Run application containers as a non-root user and use a minimal runtime image.
Rule: Validate configuration types and required fields at startup, then fail with a redacted actionable error.
Rule: Run format, lint, type checks, and static analysis in CI before merging changes.
Rule: Rotate provider credentials after suspected exposure and invalidate the previous credential immediately.
Rule: Protect local file and database mutations with transactional locking and explicit busy handling.
Decision: Keep the local control plane functional without a hosted database; remote model calls remain optional adapters.
